chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Similar to it, and there is an increase in it: 'And when you are oppressed with an injustice, be pleased with My support for you, for My support for you is better than your support for yourself.'

key_terms.مَظْلِمَة: Injustice or oppression suffered by a person

ai.seo_question: What is the benefit of being patient with God's support when oppressed?
ai.summary: In the context of al-Kulayni’s *al-Kafi*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elevates *rida* (contentment) from passive endurance to an active spiritual trust in divine justice, distinguishing between the fleeting nature of human retribution and the ultimate perfection of God's vindication. This reflects the Shia theological emphasis on *tawakkul* during times of oppression, where the believer finds peace not in the outcome of revenge, but in the certainty of Allah's superior timing and justice. The addition of 'intisar' (vindication) underscores the belief that divine intervention is not merely corrective but inherently better than self-help, aligning with the concept of *adl* (divine justice).

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali Bin Uqba, from Abdullah Bin Sinan,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, similar to it, and there is an increase in it, “And when you are oppressed with an injustice, so be please with My<sup>azwj</sup> Support for you, for My<sup>azwj</sup> Support for you is better than your support for yourself!’.
en.sarwar: 9. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from ibn Faddal from Ali ibn ‘Uqbah from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.)
a similar Hadith with the following addition: “When injustice is done to you in an oppressive condition, be happy with My support; My support for you is better than your own support for yourself.”
